phase: data volume: writable mount, write, clean unmount and read-back, all in one boot

the_bug_that_was_fixed.symptom: unmount of a volume holding a regular file never returned; the loader's 420-second budget expired and the system came back to Android
the_bug_that_was_fixed.where_it_hung: dounmount() -> vflush() -> vclean() -> ubc_destroy_named() -> memory_object_destroy() -> vm_object_destroy(), waiting for paging_in_progress to reach zero
the_bug_that_was_fixed.why_it_never_reached_zero: the driver called buf_map() on a B_CLUSTER buffer and never called buf_unmap(), so every read or write of a regular file left a reference on the file's UPL
the_bug_that_was_fixed.documented_contract: bsd/sys/buf.h:341-345 -- for a buffer created with buf_alloc() and buf_setupl(), 'buf_map() created the mapping. In this case, buf_unmap() will unmap the buffer.'
the_bug_that_was_fixed.evidence_that_pinned_it: 786 opened only a directory and unmounted cleanly; 785c (read-only, one 56-byte read), 786b, 786e and 786f all touched a regular file and all hung

changes: buf_unmap(bp) before buf_biodone(bp) on every path that mapped -- 9 places
removed the second buf_map() in the write branch; buf_map is already called before the read/write split, and mapping the same UPL twice fails
the buf_map failure branch no longer unmaps -- nothing was mapped, so there is nothing to give back

refused_512_byte_writes.symptom: unmount -> EROFS with no kernel message
refused_512_byte_writes.cause: the driver rejected any write not aligned to 4096, silently; HFS Plus writes its volume header in 512-byte pieces at offset 1024
refused_512_byte_writes.fix: read the block, lay the given bytes over the part they cover, write the whole block back
refused_512_byte_writes.proof: 786b: f_bfree 41447 -> 41446, the first time a volume header reached the flash
refused_512_byte_writes.host_test: test-rmw.c: 211 checks including 200 random offsets and lengths

the_write_ioctl_never_returned_its_resul.symptom: xnusys_hfsseed reported every block as 'not written (ok=0)' while the kernel log said ocs=0 restored=1 for all of them
the_write_ioctl_never_returned_its_resul.cause: XNUSYS_WRITE_BLOCK was _IOW, which copies the argument in and nothing back, so the driver's a->ok = 1 never reached the caller
the_write_ioctl_never_returned_its_resul.fix: _IOWR on the kernel side, 0xC0000000 in the probe
the_write_ioctl_never_returned_its_resul.note: the earlier 'verified writes' were only verified because the probe did not check ok

what_is_not_done.the_seed_probe_still_cannot_read_back: xnusys_hfsseed reads back through /dev/rxnusys, a character node bounded by the APFS container, so the window is out of its range. The writes succeed; the read-back check does not.
what_is_not_done.the_volume_is_still_not_journaled: it was journaled originally (attributes 0x80002100, JIB flags 0x5 including kJIJournalNeedInitMask) but the journal area is all zero, so a read-only mount refused it as dirty. The journal flags were cleared to get past that. Now that unmount finishes cleanly, letting the kernel run journal_create() is worth another try.
what_is_not_done.private_var_is_not_mounted_yet: the probes mount at /private/var/tmp/<name>. Mounting at /private/var itself needs init.c's mount_data_volume() and a decision about the memory disk already there

how_this_was_found.planning: a separate planning agent narrowed the hang to dounmount -> VFS_UNMOUNT after the driver's own diagnostics never printed
how_this_was_found.the_insight_that_mattered: a read-only mount that only opened a directory unmounted fine, and every mount that touched a regular file hung -- read-only or not, dirty or clean. That ruled out the dirty-page and write-path theories in one step.
how_this_was_found.decompiled_confirmation: the strategy and buf_map were executed on the host against stand-ins for the UPL and completion callbacks: with B_READ|B_CLUSTER and real_bp=NULL, ubc_upl_map was called once, buf_biodone once, and unmap zero times. The non-clustered control never entered ubc_upl_map.
